about:
Lowell Manufacturing Co is based in Pacific, Missouri. The company operates as a manufacturer of racks, power, and audio products. No founding year or ownership details are publicly disclosed.

The company produces a range of commercial audio equipment including ceiling and pendant speakers with transformers, grilles, and enclosures. It also manufactures data center and AV racks such as the DAT24 series 42U data racks, LWR wall-mount racks, LPTR4 pull-and-turn AV racks, LER enclosed AV racks, and LGR gangable AV racks. Power products include online double-conversion UPS systems with lithium batteries, line-interactive UPS with lead-acid batteries, compact standby UPS, PDUs with surge suppression and network interfaces, power sequencers, surge suppressors, and power strips. The company notes its products are "Made in USA with US and global components."

Lowell's products serve commercial audio integrators, data center operators, AV system designers, and IT infrastructure managers. Typical applications include installed sound systems in commercial buildings, education facilities, and houses of worship, as well as rack-based power distribution and backup for network equipment.

name: Luminus Devices
old_description: High-output LED chips and COB arrays for lighting, horticulture, entertainment
about:
Luminus Devices is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, where it develops and manufactures high-output LED chips and chip-on-board (COB) arrays for a range of lighting and photonics applications. The company operates as a manufacturer of illumination, specialty, and laser diode products, serving global markets through a network of local, regional, and international distributors.

Its product portfolio spans illumination LEDs for retail, hospitality, residential, industrial, outdoor, office, education, museum, and architectural settings, including circadian and human-centric lighting. Specialty lines cover ultraviolet, stage and studio, infrared, projection and display, horticulture, medical and life sciences, and automotive applications. The company also produces lasers and power products such as MOSFETs and Schottky barrier diodes. Recent releases include the SFT-70X high-CRI LED, LUX Pro and Gen6+ COB platforms, CFT-50X series for medical and industrial use, and deep-red SFT-12R and SFT-25R LEDs for stage and horticulture. Online tools such as a horticulture calculator and lumen calculators for COB and mid-power arrays support customer design work.

Luminus serves fixture manufacturers, lighting designers, and OEMs across general lighting, horticulture, entertainment, medical, life sciences, automotive, industrial, and projection/display sectors. Collaborations with partners like BluGlass, Current Chemicals, and Cuvée Systems extend its technology reach, including KSF phosphor licensing and joint driver development.

The company emphasizes efficacy, color quality, and real-world performance, citing breakthroughs such as breaking the $0.10 per milliwatt barrier for UVC LEDs and introducing Salud™ COBs with high melanopic-to-photopic ratios for healthy daytime lighting. Proprietary Robusto™ technology enables high-density COB arrays, while KSF phosphor technology enhances color rendering across its product lines.

name: Luthers Welding
old_description: Tank designs can be provided by the customer, developed in-house based on customer specifications, or reverse engineered based on existing components.
about:
Luther's Welding has operated in Bristol, Rhode Island since 1937. The business began as a small welding shop, incorporated in 1971, and two years later narrowed its focus to marine fabrication. The company remains family-owned, with each department overseen by a family member to maintain quality.

The shop provides custom metal fabrication, welding, CNC machining, and sheet metal design. Core processes include rolling, sawing, and press brake forming, allowing production of custom marine tanks (fuel, water, holding), OEM and aftermarket marine hardware such as mastheads and chain plates, and sheet metal components for utility trucks. Assembly and leak testing are performed in-house, while finishing services are sourced as needed. The facility handles projects from prototype through medium-volume runs with an emphasis on fast turnaround.

The primary customer base is the marine industry, serving boat builders and owners in the U.S. and Canada. The company also fabricates sheet metal parts for utility trucks and has produced items for various non-marine industrial clients. Tank designs can be supplied by the customer, developed in-house, or reverse engineered from existing components, and are built to American Boat and Yacht Council standards.

Luther's Welding emphasizes personal service and close customer partnerships, a byproduct of its small-company structure. The staff includes welders with decades of experience and certified qualifications, supported by a machine shop and engineering department each with over 35 years of expertise. The family oversight model is intended to ensure that every product leaving the facility meets the company's reputation for reliability.

name: Lutron Electronics
old_description: Manufactures lighting control switches, dimmers, and shading systems.
about:
Lutron Electronics was founded in 1961 in Coopersburg, Pennsylvania. The privately held company began as a manufacturer of lighting control devices and has since expanded into shading systems and building automation.

The company produces a range of lighting controls including dimmers, switches, keypads, remotes, and sensors, as well as motorized shades, drapery, and blinds under the Sivoia brand. Its control systems — such as HomeWorks, RadioRA3, Athena, Vive, and myRoom XC — serve residential, commercial, and hospitality projects. Lutron also offers embedded fixture technology for OEM integration. The firm provides commercial project support encompassing design and specification services, installation support, system verification, and technical startup assistance.

Lutron serves architects, builders, electrical contractors, engineers, interior designers, lighting dealers, and facility managers across residential, commercial, and hospitality sectors. Notable projects include the BlackRock headquarters, SOM offices, Hotel Indigo Dubai, Sofitel Rome, Banyan Tree Hotel, The Ritz-Carlton, Taliesin West, and the Stay Bungalow.

The company emphasizes wireless technology that enables design freedom and performance beyond traditional wired controls, along with automated glare and thermal management that preserves exterior views. Its systems integrate lighting, window treatments, and smart-home functionality into a single platform.

name: Lydia Design Studio
old_description: We are a leading clothing production company based in Atlanta, GA, offering top-quality clothing and supporting the domestic apparel manufacturing industry in the USA.
about:
Lydia Design Studio operates from Atlanta, Georgia, where head designer Lydia founded the company to provide domestic apparel manufacturing services. The studio positions itself as a boutique operation offering personalized attention from concept through finished goods.

The company delivers end-to-end cut-and-sew production entirely in-house. Its workflow covers design consultation, hand sketching, pattern-making, sample development, fabric cutting, sewing, printing, finishing, and a three-stage inspection process at pre-cut, mid-sew, and post-finish stages. Product categories include t-shirts, leggings, jeans, hoodies, jackets, underwear, and sweatshirts, all customizable with custom labels, tags, and packaging.

Clients range from startup fashion brands to established clothing companies and film studios seeking made-in-USA garments. The studio emphasizes low minimum order quantities to accommodate emerging labels while also serving larger production runs.

Lydia Design Studio differentiates itself through boutique-level care, competitive pricing relative to New York and Los Angeles manufacturers, a commitment to eco-friendly and sustainable materials, and fast turnaround times. The founder, Lydia, personally oversees each project to ensure quality and alignment with the client's vision.

name: M. Joseph Medical
old_description: Injured workers pay no out-of-pocket expenses through our national network of pharmacies & mail-order channels.
about:
M. Joseph Medical was founded in 1985 in Louisville, Kentucky, as a durable medical equipment supplier to the workers' compensation payer community. The company has operated as an employee-owned business since its inception, a structure it credits for steady, controllable growth without the mergers, acquisitions, or high turnover that have affected competitors.

Today the firm provides pharmacy benefit management (PBM) and durable medical equipment (DME) services on a national scale. Its pharmacy solutions include a nationwide network of retail and mail-order pharmacies that allow injured workers to fill prescriptions with no out-of-pocket expense. Ancillary offerings span disposable medical products, translation and transportation services, home health care, electrotherapy, and catastrophic claim support. The company also issues first-fill and Rx cards to streamline medication access.

The primary customers are workers' compensation payers — insurance carriers, third-party administrators, and self-insured employers — who rely on M. Joseph Medical to manage pharmacy and ancillary benefits for injured workers. The company also serves a national network of pharmacies that participate in its mail-order and retail channels.

Leadership says the employee-ownership model aligns incentives toward long-term service quality rather than short-term financial engineering. By avoiding external ownership changes, the firm maintains consistent staffing and institutional knowledge, which it says translates into higher care standards and competitive pricing for its payer clients.

name: MAC Plastics Manufacturing,Inc.
old_description: Our customer service includes quality engineering & production, but also finding solutions to other customer needs such as timing, packaging and warehousing.
about:
MAC Plastics Manufacturing, Inc. is headquartered in Olney, Illinois, with a second production facility in Hamilton, Indiana added in 2022. The company was founded by Rod Michels, Aaron Ackman, and Brian Craig, drawing on over 75 years of combined plastics experience among its leadership. In 2019, an ownership group acquired the business, maintaining a family-oriented culture focused on custom manufacturing and dependable delivery.

The company produces custom plastic extrusions, co-extrusions, injection molded parts, tooling, fabrication, finishing, and assemblies. Operations span two Midwest facilities totaling over 100,000 square feet, equipped with 20 extrusion lines, six co-extrusion lines, and three injection molding machines. Inline capabilities include punching, cutting, notching, drilling, boring, chamfering, and printing; offline secondary operations cover CNC routing, custom packaging, assembly, and warehousing. Engineering support, 3D-printed prototyping, and testing to ASTM and IAPMO standards round out the production depth.

MAC serves OEMs, distributors, public utilities, and industrial buyers across aerospace, defense, agriculture, marine and pool, lawn and garden, telecommunications, construction, industrial manufacturing, transportation, sanitation, utilities, and energy sectors. A noted specialty is co-extruded rigid and flexible trailing shields for the walk-behind mower industry.

The company emphasizes lean production discipline, in-house tooling, and practical engineering to deliver parts built to customer drawings rather than off-the-shelf. Leadership cites a team-driven culture of continuous improvement, competitive positioning, and attention to timing, packaging, and real-world fit as core differentiators.

name: MBC Food Machinery Corporation
old_description: MBC has been providing innovative machinery solutions to the frozen food industry since 1965.
about:
MBC Food Machinery Corporation is based in Hackensack, New Jersey, and has been operating since 1965. The privately held company was founded to serve the frozen food sector and has remained under continuous ownership for nearly six decades.

The company designs and builds custom high‑production equipment for the frozen‑filled pasta market, including machines that form ravioli, manicotti, cannelloni, stuffed shells, cavatelli, pierogie, stuffed rigatoni and lasagna. All machinery is manufactured at its Hackensack facility using CAD‑driven processes and materials that meet USDA standards, and each unit is tested before shipment. MBC also runs a full‑service machine shop offering CNC machining, CNC turning, welding and fabrication, and it provides machinery rebuilding services for both domestic and imported equipment. In addition, the firm maintains a stock of replacement parts for immediate dispatch and offers plant‑layout consulting to help customers optimize production space.

MBC’s primary customers are frozen‑food manufacturers in the United States, Canada and Europe that produce filled pasta products. The company’s equipment and services are tailored to high‑volume production lines in the frozen pasta segment.

MBC traces its industry leadership to the introduction of the first automatic manicotti‑cannelloni production line nearly 50 years ago. The company emphasizes U.S.‑based manufacturing, rigorous USDA‑compliant construction, quick‑ship replacement parts designed for easy on‑site changeover, and personalized design services for custom applications — factors it says underpin long‑term customer relationships.

name: MCC Electronics
old_description: Proudly serving customers in Kansas City and around the world since 1972
about:
Mid-Continent Custom Electronics (MCCE), operating as MCC Electronics, is headquartered in Lee's Summit, Missouri, in the Kansas City metropolitan area. The company was founded in 1972 and has served customers globally from its domestic base for over five decades. In 2012, Mark Dohnalek acquired Pivot International, the global design, engineering, and manufacturing firm that owns MCCE as a subsidiary. Pivot International maintains offices in the United Kingdom and Hong Kong, with additional manufacturing plants in Kansas City and Asia, giving MCCE access to global resources while retaining U.S. production.

MCCE provides single-source original design manufacturing (ODM) and electronic manufacturing services (EMS) for electronic and electro-mechanical products. Its capabilities span hardware design, circuit board layout and assembly (both surface-mount and through-hole), embedded software development, mechanical engineering, and industrial design. The domestic facility handles prototyping, low-volume runs, and high-volume production, performing electro-mechanical panel and box assembly, device programming, custom silkscreening, encapsulating, conformal coating, and in-house test fixture construction. All products undergo 100% inspection at the U.S. plant.

The company serves a diverse industrial base, including unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), agricultural equipment such as combines and hay balers, construction machinery like boom lifts, fire and emergency vehicle door systems, airport and corporate intercom control panels, hospital and detention center security systems, livestock and veterinary scales, and isokinetic exercise data logging. Customers range from OEMs needing full product development to those requiring contract assembly or design rescue.

MCCE emphasizes its domestic manufacturing oversight, global supply chain reach through Pivot International, and award-winning design team as key differentiators. The firm positions itself as a partner that can take a concept through to production, reduce costs on legacy products, improve quality, and recover troubled projects.
